transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… thank you. I guess I’m here because I’ve noticed I’m not really… reaching for life the way I used to. That sounds dramatic, sorry. I’m still doing what I need to do, work and basic obligations, but the part of me that used to enjoy people, my work, yoga, going to galleries, even journaling—it’s all gotten very quiet. I don’t feel as pulled toward any of it. I thought maybe I should talk to someone before I just keep pushing through.
Has this loss of interest felt like a distinct change from your usual self?

Yes… I think it has. I mean, I’m still functioning, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But it does feel different from me. I used to naturally reach out to people, feel interested in my work, go to yoga, want to see galleries, write things down… and now that part just feels very quiet. Mostly I’m just getting through the things I’m supposed to do.
Along with losing interest in things, have you been feeling down or depressed?

I don’t know that I’d call it depressed, exactly. Maybe a little flat? But not… I mean, I’m not falling apart or anything. It’s more like the interest has faded than that I’m sad all the time, if that makes sense.
How long have you been feeling this loss of interest?

I think… about eight months? It kind of started around when we took my older relative into our apartment. I don’t want to overstate it, but since then this whole shift in how I’m thinking, working, and connecting with people has been there. So, yes—around eight months.
Do you feel these changes began because of the stress of your older relative moving into your apartment?

I mean… I don’t want to blame it all on that, because that feels a little unfair. But the timing does line up. This whole change in how I’m thinking, working, and connecting with people has been going on for about eight months, since we took my older relative into our apartment. So… yes, maybe the stress had something to do with it? I’m not completely sure.
Is your older relative still living with you?

I’m… not totally sure how to answer that neatly. I mean, the living situation has been a little fluid, and I don’t want to give you the wrong impression. They’ve been around a lot, but whether I’d say “still living with us” exactly… I’d have to think about how to put it.
For most of the past eight months, have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless?

I’m not sure I’d call it depressed, exactly. Maybe that’s me trying to put it in a better light, but… I haven’t been feeling great. More kind of flat or worn down at times. Hopeless sounds a little strong to me, though. I don’t know if that answers what you’re asking.
If your older relative were no longer staying with you, do you think you’d still feel this way?

I’d like to think it would get better if the house were calmer… maybe it would, some. But honestly, I’m not sure it’s only about them being there. What finally made me come in is that the part of me that used to reach out to people, or really enjoy my work, yoga, going to galleries, even journaling… it’s just gotten very quiet. I’m still doing what I have to do, mostly, but it feels more like moving through obligations than actually feeling connected to any of it. Does that make sense?
Have you had trouble sleeping?

A little, maybe… I don’t think it’s terrible. I sometimes take longer to settle down, or I wake up and then start thinking, but I’m still getting some sleep. I don’t want to overstate it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Before these past eight months, had you already been feeling this kind of low interest or flatness for at least two years?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had stressful periods before, like anyone, but this particular change… the way I’m thinking and working and connecting with people feeling different, that’s really been more like the last eight months, since we took my older relative into our apartment. So not two years, as far as I can tell.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?
I don’t think so… not in any clear way. I’m eating, maybe not always with much enthusiasm, but I haven’t noticed a big change in appetite or anything that would worry me. Does that sound relevant?
During these past eight months, have you often felt sad?

Not really “sad,” no… or at least I wouldn’t call it that. Maybe a little discouraged here and there, but I don’t feel like I’ve been crying or feeling down all the time. I’m trying to answer that accurately—sad doesn’t quite feel like the right word.
Have you been under unusual stress at work during these past eight months?

A little, yes… though I don’t want to make it sound dramatic. I’m still going in and doing my job, but I haven’t been at my usual level. I’ve missed a couple of grant deadlines, which is embarrassing, and my supervisor has… kind of quietly shifted some of my more demanding clients to other clinicians. I think she’s trying to be supportive, but it does make me wonder if it’s more noticeable than I want it to be.
Because of these changes, has your functioning been noticeably impaired?

I suppose… yes, but I’d say mildly. I’m still showing up to work and trying to keep things moving, so it’s not like I’ve completely fallen apart. But I have missed a couple of grant deadlines, and my supervisor has sort of quietly moved some of the more demanding clients to other clinicians. I think because I’m just not functioning at my usual level. I don’t know if that counts as “noticeably,” but… yes, probably.
For most of the past eight months, have you felt depressed most days?

I don’t think I’d say depressed most days, no. I mean, I’ve had off days, and I’ve been worried about not doing as well as I should, but “depressed” feels a little stronger than what I’ve noticed. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low in energy?

Not unusually, I don’t think. I mean, I get tired like anyone does, especially after work, but I haven’t really noticed it as a main problem. I’m still managing to get through the day. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

I’m not sure I’d call it trouble concentrating exactly. I mean, maybe I’m a little slower to settle into things than I used to be, but I can still focus when I really need to. So… not in a major way, I don’t think. Does that answer it?
Did these changes continue for more than six months after your older relative stopped staying with you?

Well… I guess the timing is a little different. The changes have been going on about eight months altogether, but it started when we took my older relative into our apartment. So I’m not sure I’d say it was more than six months after they stopped staying with us—more that it’s been around eight months since that began. Does that make sense?
Before this started eight months ago, have you ever had another period like this?

I don’t think so… not like this, anyway. I mean, I’ve had stressful stretches before, like most people, but I can’t really point to another period that felt the same as these last eight months. Does that help?
Have these changes been causing you a lot of emotional distress?

I wouldn’t say a lot, no. It’s been… upsetting at times, I guess, but I’ve been trying to handle it and keep perspective. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Maybe some stress, but not overwhelming. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
